title: Temporal solitons
title_note: Read from the arXiv preprint (arXiv:1211.0733v3, 2013) of Herr et al., "Temporal solitons in optical microresonators", Nature Photonics 8, 145-152 (2014); page and figure locators are those of the preprint. The paper reports "the observation of temporal dissipative solitons in a high-Q optical microresonator" and makes no "first" claim for them. The later name "dissipative Kerr soliton" is not used in the paper.
tagline: Pulses form by themselves in a crystalline MgF_{2} microresonator.

parts.name: MgF_{2} microresonator
parts.role: The smaller resonator; light runs round its rim.
parts.detail: Whispering-gallery-mode resonator with Kerr nonlinearity and anomalous dispersion, the two requirements the authors name for soliton formation. FSR 35.2 GHz; coupled resonance width κ/2π = 450 kHz, measured with modulation sidebands of a scanning laser (Q = 4×10^{8}). Measured dispersion D_{2}/2π = 16 kHz (β_{2} = -9.39 ps^{2} km^{-1}, Fig. 1b); D_{3} and higher terms negligible. Diameter not stated: c / (π n_{0} FSR) gives about 1.98 mm (n_{0} used in place of the unstated group index), consistent with the about 2.0 mm top tier in Fig. 1a. Estimated A_{eff} = 90×10^{-12} m^{2}, V_{eff} = 5.6×10^{-13} m^{3}, n_{2} = 0.9×10^{-20} m^{2}/W, γ = 4.1×10^{-4} m^{-1}W^{-1}.
parts.quote: The microresonator is characterized by a free-spectral range (FSR) of 35.2 GHz (Fig. 1a and Methods) and a coupled resonance width of 450 kHz.
parts.locator: Herr et al., arXiv v3 (2013), p.2; p.5 Methods; p.7 Fig. 1a, 1b

parts.name: Scan
parts.role: Tunes the pump to lower optical frequency across the resonance.
parts.detail: The laser is scanned "with decreasing optical frequency ω_{p} over a high-Q resonance". Coming from the blue side, the resonance self-locks to the laser (thermal triangle); tuning on through the effective zero detuning reaches the red-detuned side where the solitons form. To stop in a chosen soliton state the scan speed is set so that the resonator temperature matches that state (SI Fig. 6). The scan span in frequency for Fig. 2a is not stated (axis in scan time only).
parts.quote: we scan a pump laser (fiber laser; wavelength 1553 nm; linewidth ∼ 10 kHz) with decreasing optical frequency ωp over a high-Q resonance of the crystalline MgF2 resonator
parts.locator: Herr et al., arXiv v3 (2013), p.2; p.3; p.18 Fig. 6

parts.name: soliton pulse
parts.role: Short pulse circulating on a weak continuous background.
parts.detail: Simulation (Fig. 3c, e): the first step turns the modulated intracavity waveform into several pulses; each further step leaves fewer; the separation between pulses is random. Eq. (1) describes them as sech pulses on a cw background; the peak to background power ratio "can typically exceed several hundreds". Fig. 1c insets (schematic): random comb phases give no pulse, synchronized phases give one pulse. Experiment: states with one, two and five solitons (Fig. 4). The paper does not state the number of solitons on each step of Fig. 2a. Later work: Brasch et al. (Science 2016, read from arXiv v2) reach soliton states in a silicon nitride (SiN) ring, 238 µm across, where soliton Cherenkov radiation widens the comb to 2/3 of an octave with pulses below 30 fs.
parts.quote: Further steps can be associated with a stepwise reduction of the number of pulses propagating in the resonator.
parts.locator: Herr et al., arXiv v3 (2013), p.3; p.7 Fig. 1c; p.9 Fig. 3c, 3e; later work Brasch et al., arXiv v2 (2015), p.1, p.2, p.4

parts.name: output pulse train
parts.role: One pulse leaves through the fiber each roundtrip.
parts.detail: Single soliton: smooth sech^{2} spectral envelope, 3 dB bandwidth 1.6 THz (more than 45 modes); with a time-bandwidth product of 0.315 the expected duration is 197 fs. Frequency-resolved optical gating (FROG) reconstructs 200 fs FWHM (error 1.7 %) and shows pulses spaced by T_{R} = 28.4 ps. A temporal magnifier (x105.5, about 2.5 ps resolution, single shot) shows pulses spaced by T_{R} with constant amplitude. Before these measurements the pump is suppressed (-30 dB, FBG), the light amplified to 50 mW and roughly dispersion compensated; no other spectral filtering or phase adjustment.
parts.quote: the reconstructed temporal width of 200 fs (FWHM) is in agreement with the bandwidth of the optical spectrum and the expectation based on eq. (2)

chapters.line: A disc of crystalline MgF_{2} holds the light.
chapters.action: plain disc stand-in for the resonator (diameter derived from the FSR, drawn not to scale) on a plain post stand-in for the crystal; tiers and fabrication not drawn; never called machined

chapters.line: Light circles the rim, once per roundtrip.
chapters.action: view moves to the top tier in a tilted (isometric) view; a faint ring of light runs round just inside the rim (one loop = one roundtrip); canvas label FSR and Q on the resonator

chapters.line: A tapered fiber couples pump light in and out.
chapters.action: a plain fiber line slides in and touches the rim tangentially with a thin waist (Fig. 2d draws the thinning); light from the left leaks into the ring and the rest continues to the right; no taper size or gap drawn

chapters.line: Amplified fiber laser in; spectrum, transmission and beat note out.
chapters.action: zoom out to the Fig. 2d layout: pump laser + EDFA box with the scan box, FPC paddles, fiber to the taper at the resonator, output fiber down to three branches: OSA; PD to oscilloscope; FBG, PD, LO mixer to ESA with a branch to the oscilloscope. Canvas label: pump wavelength

chapters.line: Tuned past zero detuning, the transmission climbs in discrete steps.
chapters.action: model (resonator + taper close-up) on the left, plot right. The drive is the plotted scan time: a marker on the pump wavelength moves with the pen (0 to 4 ms; never past 4 ms). Output-fiber brightness follows the digitized transmission at the pen. Intracavity ring: 0-0.5 ms dim (off resonance); 0.5-3.1 ms ring brightens as transmission falls (thermal triangle, laser on the blue side); comb sidebands at the pen positions I (1.50 ms), II (1.96 ms), III (2.72 ms) as faint side tints, flickering noisy waveform from about 1.5 ms (high-noise beat, Fig. 2c); at 3.12 ms (first step) the noise collapses into several sharp pulses on the ring; at the steps (3.55, 3.65, 3.76, 3.86 ms) the pulse count drops. Pulse counts on the ring are illustrative (hover: the paper does not state them for Fig. 2a; simulation Fig. 3c shows fewer pulses per step)

chapters.line: One soliton circulates; each roundtrip couples one pulse out.
chapters.action: plot leaves; close-up of the ring: one sharp sech pulse on a dim cw background circles the rim; each pass at the taper sends a short pulse along the output fiber, pulses spaced evenly (spacing and width schematic; hover T_{R} = 28.4 ps, 200 fs); Fig. 1c right inset is the schematic basis

chapters.line: A single soliton gives a smooth sech^{2} spectrum.
chapters.action: model left (one pulse circling, pulse train on the fiber), plot right: one-soliton spectrum assembles left to right, then the dashed sech^{2} envelope; alternates two and five solitons (structured spectra)

chapters.line: Frequency-resolved optical gating reconstructs the pulse.
chapters.action: model left (pulse train on the fiber), plot right: reconstructed intensity, then the dashed sech^{2} curve; alternate: sampled intensity with two pulses one roundtrip apart (temporal magnifier)

plots.source: Herr et al., arXiv v3 (2013), p.8, Fig. 2a: 'Transmission observed when scanning a laser over a high-Q Kerr-nonlinear resonance in a MgF2 resonator (coupled pump power 5 mW).'
plots.note: Measured transmission while the pump is scanned to lower optical frequency (coupled pump power 5 mW). Digitized from the vector trace of Fig. 2a: first, lowest, highest and last trace vertex in each 1/200 of the time axis, so the noise band keeps its edges and the steps stay sharp. Spectra I, II, III of Fig. 2b were taken at 1.50, 1.96 and 2.72 ms; the first step (3.12 ms) marks the transition to a narrow beat note and solitons; the narrow beat note ends at the last step (about 3.86 ms, Fig. 2c).
